correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, positive normalized stationary masses and positive edge prices, the path covariance identity supplies Var_pi(f)=d^T G d with strictly positive G_ij. Testing the sqrt-price position vector yields universal gap <=1/D. Positive rates w_i=(Gg)_i/(Dg_i) obey the exact cost budget, and an exact nonnegative sum-of-squares identity proves every feasible edge-gradient Rayleigh quotient >=1/D. Equality conditions prove spectral simplicity. Any other optimizer must attain the same test-vector Rayleigh bound and satisfy the generalized eigenvector equation, whose telescoping vertex equations force each w_i uniquely. Different finite-boundary cases (including n=2) are handled. Standalone exact verifier: 801 instances/6408 Gram identities, plus separate 420 nonsquare-price eigen comparisons; all supplementary, not substituted for universal proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The first three antecedents have broader topology but strictly narrower allowed input parameters; their uniform-mass/uniform-price tree solution is a proper special case of the new path statement, not an implication proving its full parameter family. The Shafi general numerical formulation can *encode* the present case, so the overlap is acknowledged; it does not give the claimed exact answer, all-rate formula, or O(n) construction. A general optimization framework is not itself a closed-form solution to each instance.

originality.rationale: The exact simultaneous heterogeneous stationary-mass and heterogeneous edge-price closed form is not supplied by the inspected primary uniform-mass/unit-price tree theorems or by broader semidefinite-programming frameworks. Fiedler 1990 and Göring–Helmberg–Wappler 2005 cover the unit-price/unit-mass specialization, while Wan et al. 2008 give an algorithm for uniform tree edge design. Shafi et al. 2010 formulate general node/edge spectral semidefinite problems but give neither this sharp weighted-path formula nor its exact rate flux and uniqueness. Boyd et al. 2006 optimize a different discrete-time objective. The answer is not claimed to be absolutely novel on search absence alone: Fiedler 1990 is available only as an abstract, and unknown equivalents remain a genuine risk.
residual_risks: Fiedler (1990) original full article remained unavailable after lawful open-access searches; its abstract clearly describes uniform valuation, but unobserved sections might contain a more general mass/price variant. Institutional-access attempt did not yield material.

General weighted graph SDP frameworks can express the problem without giving the closed form; an earlier independent specialization with the same exact mass/price formulas could exist under different terminology.
Database and literature searches do not cover unpublished work; novelty is a supported bounded assessment, not proof of priority.

value.rationale: The simultaneous arbitrary positive stationary masses and individual edge prices form a natural fixed-resource fastest-relaxation problem for reversible birth-death dynamics. The fully quantified optimum is an explicit weighted price-metric variance, not just existence of an SDP solution; all positive conductances are uniquely obtained by an O(n) flux calculation, with spectral simplicity and exact marginal price sensitivities. This is a complete continuous-parameter classification of a motivated design object, not an arbitrary finite slice or a recomputation of Fiedler’s uniform-mass/cost specialization. Nonpath, discrete-time, and nonlinear budgets are expressly not claimed.
